title: A smaller studio, better used
subtitle: A proposal for two workstations, shared storage and a little more space between them.

pages.title: The proposal
pages.markdown:
![A bright workspace with a shared desk, plants and natural light](./assets/studio.webp "Reference interior · Photograph by FlippingBook / Unsplash")

Keep the room. Change the furniture. The proposal is to replace the mismatched desks with **one shared work surface**, move storage to the back wall and leave the centre of the room clear.

### What this solves

The current arrangement makes it difficult to work side by side or move through the room when both desks are in use. Buying more furniture would make that worse.

The new arrangement should provide:

- Two permanent workstations, with **power and cables kept off the floor**.
- One storage point for equipment that is currently spread across the room.
- A small reading corner that can double as a place for informal conversations.

> [!NOTE]
> This is an illustrative proposal. Costs below are planning allowances, not supplier quotes.

### The important constraint

We need to keep the existing room and avoid structural work. The reference photograph is a direction for the furniture and light, *not a promise about the finished space*.

[View the reference photograph and its source](https://unsplash.com/photos/modern-office-space-with-plants-and-desk-_XbcXekBecY).

pages.title: Layout & budget
pages.markdown:
![A simple room plan with a shared desk by the window, storage on the back wall and a clear central area](./assets/studio-plan.webp "Proposed arrangement · Illustration, not a measured floor plan")

### Compare the options

| Option | What changes | Planning allowance | Trade-off |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| Keep the current desks | Reposition furniture and tidy cables | £150 | Least disruption; limited improvement |
| **Shared work surface** | New desk, storage and cable management | **£950** | Requires a day to clear and reset the room |
| Separate fitted workstations | Custom furniture for each position | £1,800 | Better fit; larger commitment before testing |

The shared surface is the preferred option because it can be tried without commissioning fitted furniture.

### Suggested allowance

- Shared desk or worktop: **£450**
- Closed storage: **£250**
- Cable trays, power and small fittings: **£100**
- Delivery and contingency: **£150**

**Total: £950.** Check room measurements and supplier prices before ordering.

---

### What stays

1. Existing chairs, if they remain comfortable at the new desk height.
2. The reading light and shelves.
3. The current electrical installation; an electrician should assess any changes to sockets.

pages.title: Before we order
pages.markdown:
### Preparation checklist

- [x] Choose a preferred arrangement.
- [x] Set a provisional spending limit.
- [ ] Measure the room, door clearance and desk height.
- [ ] Check the position and capacity of existing sockets.
- [ ] Obtain quotes for the desk and storage.
- [ ] Agree a day when the room can be cleared.

### Sequence

1. **Measure first.** Mark the proposed desk footprint on the floor with tape.
2. **Try the arrangement.** Move the existing furniture to approximate the new layout.
3. **Order only after the trial.** Check that two people can work comfortably and reach the storage.
4. **Review after a week.** Adjust the small details before buying anything else.

> [!TIP]
> A taped outline is a cheaper way to spot a bad fit than a delivery you need to return.

### Decision requested

Approve the layout trial and the provisional **£950** limit. Ordering remains conditional on measurements and actual quotes.
